pr_title: ES|QL: fix stats by constant expresson with alias
pr_body:
Fix planning of queries with STATS and grouping aliases

```
FROM test
| EVAL y = \"a\"
| STATS COUNT() BY x=y
| SORT x
```

`x` is now excluded from the references list (it's a generated value), so that the index resolution happens correctly.

Fixes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/114714

issue_context.title: ESQL: STATS BY expression not working with expression from EVAL
issue_context.body: `FROM employees | eval x = [1,2,3], y = 5 + 6 | stats by y + 1` or `FROM employees | eval x = [1,2,3], y = 5 + 6 | stats by yy = y + 1` currently return 0 rows, even though using expressions in the `by` clause works fine if they use only fields that are present in the index. Using `by` clauses composed from both index fields and eval fields seems to work, too, like `FROM test | eval x = [1,2,3], y = 5 + 6 | stats by yy = y + a`.
comments:
I think the problem may be in either `SkipQueryOnEmptyMappings` or in `PropagateEmptyRelation`; that's from the optimizer passes:

```

...

[2024-10-14T14:49:39,880][INFO ][o.e.x.e.o.LogicalPlanOptimizer] [runTask-0] Rule logical.SkipQueryOnEmptyMappings applied
Limit[1000[INTEGER]]                                                = Limit[1000[INTEGER]]
\_Aggregate[STANDARD,[y + 1{r}#41],[y + 1{r}#41]]                   = \_Aggregate[STANDARD,[y + 1{r}#41],[y + 1{r}#41]]
  \_Eval[[y{r}#39 + 1[INTEGER] AS y + 1]]                           =   \_Eval[[y{r}#39 + 1[INTEGER] AS y + 1]]
    \_Eval[[[1, 2, 3][INTEGER] AS x, 5[INTEGER] + 6[INTEGER] AS y]] =     \_Eval[[[1, 2, 3][INTEGER] AS x, 5[INTEGER] + 6[INTEGER] AS y]]

[2024-10-14T14:49:39,880][INFO ][o.e.x.e.o.LogicalPlanOptimizer] [runTask-0] Rule logical.CombineEvals applied
Limit[1000[INTEGER]]                                                = Limit[1000[INTEGER]]
\_Aggregate[STANDARD,[y + 1{r}#41],[y + 1{r}#41]]                   = \_Aggregate[STANDARD,[y + 1{r}#41],[y + 1{r}#41]]
  \_Eval[[y{r}#39 + 1[INTEGER] AS y + 1]]                           !   \_Eval[[[1, 2, 3][INTEGER] AS x, 5[INTEGER] + 6[INTEGER] AS y, y{r}#39 + 1[INTEGER] AS y + 1]]

      \_LocalRelation[[<no-fields>{r$}#10],EMPTY]                   ! 
                                                                   
[2024-10-14T14:49:39,880][INFO ][o.e.x.e.o.LogicalPlanOptimizer] [runTask-0] Rule logical.PropagateEmptyRelation applied
Limit[1000[INTEGER]]                                                                             = Limit[1000[INTEGER]]
\_Aggregate[STANDARD,[y + 1{r}#41],[y + 1{r}#41]]                                                = \_Aggregate[STANDARD,[y + 1{r}#41],[y + 1{r}#41]]
  \_Eval[[[1, 2, 3][INTEGER] AS x, 5[INTEGER] + 6[INTEGER] AS y, y{r}#39 + 1[INTEGER] AS y + 1]] !   \_LocalRelation[[<no-fields>{r$}#10, x{r}#37, y{r}#39, y + 1{r}#41],EMPTY]
    \_LocalRelation[[<no-fields>{r$}#10],EMPTY]                                                  ! 
                                                                                                
[2024-10-14T14:49:39,880][INFO ][o.e.x.e.o.LogicalPlanOptimizer] [runTask-0] Rule logical.PropagateEmptyRelation applied
Limit[1000[INTEGER]]                                                         = Limit[1000[INTEGER]]
\_Aggregate[STANDARD,[y + 1{r}#41],[y + 1{r}#41]]                            ! \_LocalRelation[[y + 1{r}#41],EMPTY]
  \_LocalRelation[[<no-fields>{r$}#10, x{r}#37, y{r}#39, y + 1{r}#41],EMPTY] ! 

...
```
We seem to end up with an empty local relation - but we should have 1 row instead.

At a first look, the problem seems to be at a lower level, in the IndexResolver. 
In a query with `STATS by y` the EsIndex has one concrete index, while in a query with `STATS by y + 1` the EsIndex has no concrete indices, so `SkipQueryOnEmptyMappings` replaces it with a `LocalRelation`.

Digging a bit deeper, I see that the real difference is in `Aggregate.computeReferences()`: 
- for `STATS by y` it only returns `y`as an UnresolvedAttribute
- for `STATS by y + 1` it returns `y`, but also `y + 1`, the implicit - artificial aggregate of the STATS (that internally looks like `STATS y + 1 by y + 1`). 

In the first case, `y` gets removed later, and to make things work we add `_index` field to make the field_caps work.
In the second case, `y` gets removed, but not `y + 1`, so we don't add `_index`, but since `y + 1` does't match any fields in the schema, `field_caps` returns an empty list of indices.

A simple solution (and IMHO correct) could be to remove these implicit aggregates from `Aggregate.computeReferences()`
cc @alex-spies @astefan

Reopening, as the bug still occurs when there's a command using the grouping attribute alias after the aggregation.
Like:
```
FROM test
| EVAL y = \"a\"
| STATS COUNT() BY x=y
| SORT x
```
This will return no rows.

Remove the alias, and it will work, like:
```
FROM test
| EVAL y = \"a\"
| STATS COUNT() BY y
| SORT y
```

Edit with some details found while investigating:
Apparently this part, which is supposed to remove the "generated" aliases, is entering the `if` instead for such aliases: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/32aaacbd7b383188f2b5eb64fce69a09d11bfc94/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/session/EsqlSession.java#L516-L521

review_comments:
Plans have logic to correctly calculate their references, no need to reinvent the wheel here.

In general, IMHO this method is trying to do too much.
The logic should be simple: each plan should declare needed inputs and produced outputs; this method should just start from the top of the plan, visit it down and for each plan node 
- remove the outputs 
- add the required inputs. 

All the `instanceof` above should be encapsulated in the single logical plan classes.

Ideally, yes. I was about to suggest a refactor of `fieldNames` to make things simpler and more local, similarly to what you described.

However, since we're at a point here where references are not yet resolved, we cannot use the existing query plan methods as we would wish. Esp. the plan's `output` and `outputSet` methods _do not work_ here because these require resolved references, and also need to know about what fields are even present in relations. This, and the fact that we _need to match references by name_ rather than by _id_. This prevents us from just using the simple approach from [ProjectAwayColumns](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/a245e709ba5a94ad7a476a84d43f0b04bd361fc4/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/optimizer/rules/physical/ProjectAwayColumns.java#L82-L84).

However, using the `references` method should be okay at this point because that's something that can be determined locally for a plan node.
